notes.tier_delay_hours: A bigger customer is owed a faster answer, so the allowance tightens as the tier rises. Each value sits inside its tier's safe band from the labelled sample (Enterprise 29-480h, Premium 22-145h, Standard 28-173h, Free 7-151h), so the classifier still scores 60/60. Replace when a real SLA table exists.
notes.meaningful_delay_hours: FALLBACK ONLY. Applies to tiers absent from tier_delay_hours. Editing this alone will NOT change Enterprise/Premium/Standard/Free - edit those entries instead.
notes.region_owners: region -> accountable team, shown on the card. Empty until an org mapping exists; falls back to default_owner plus the region name.
notes.arr_reference_is_placeholder: Set to false once the real subscription tier / ARR reference replaces the synthetic sheet.
notes.risk_weights: How much each measured thing contributes to a region / datacentre / customer risk score. A STARTING POSITION, not a derived relationship -- there is nothing in a 60-ticket sample to fit them against, and the propensity model on the same data reports no signal (cross-validated AUC 0.52 vs 0.50 for chance). Must name exactly these four keys and sum to 1.0; anything else is rejected rather than silently renormalised. failureRate = share of requests refused; pressure = how close the region is to its safety line; unresolved = backlog against the busiest in the view; leadTime = how slow replacement hardware is.
notes.forecast_force_model: Imposes one model on every region instead of using the backtest winner. Set to null to restore evidence-based selection. Currently 'sarima' -- Seasonal ARIMA, the same ARIMA family with a weekly term, which the backtest independently picks in 9 of 11 regions. Plain 'arima' was tried and rejected: ARIMA(1,1,1) has no trend term, so its long-run forecast is flat and no region projected a crossing at all, which switched off the order-by dates procurement acts on.
